title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Ytterbium (Yb, Z=70) is 173.054(5)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Ytterbium (Yb, Z=70) as 173.054(5), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 70, symbol Yb, as Ytterbium. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Ytterbium as 173.054(5). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. Geological materials are known in which the element has an isotopic composition outside the limits for normal material. The difference between the atomic weight of the element in such materials and that given in the table may exceed the stated uncertainty. Isotope rows in the same file: Yb-168 relative atomic mass 167.9338896(22), isotopic composition 0.00123(3); Yb-170 relative atomic mass 169.9347664(22), isotopic composition 0.02982(39); Yb-171 relative atomic mass 170.9363302(22), isotopic composition 0.1409(14); Yb-172 relative atomic mass 171.9363859(22), isotopic composition 0.2168(13); Yb-173 relative atomic mass 172.9382151(22), isotopic composition 0.16103(63); Yb-174 relative atomic mass 173.9388664(22), isotopic composition 0.32026(80); Yb-176 relative atomic mass 175.9425764(24), isotopic composition 0.12996(83). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
